chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Zareeh who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'The night prayer was missed by me during the journey, so can I fulfil it during the day?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, if you can bear it'.
ai.seo_question: Can the missed night prayer be made up during the day while traveling?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the missed night prayer (Salat al-Layl) is not strictly bound to nighttime, allowing it to be made up during the day if the traveler is physically capable ('if you can bear it'). This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on practicality and ease (Yusr) in voluntary acts of worship, distinguishing them from obligatory prayers which have fixed times. It underscores the flexibility granted to travelers in maintaining spiritual discipline without undue hardship.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Zareeh who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘The night Salāt was missed out by me during the journey, so can I fulfil it during the day?’ So heasws said: ‘Yes, if you can bear it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from Dharih who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about nightly optional Salah (prayer) which are missed. Can I perform the compensatory prayer for them during the day? He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, you can do so, if you are able to bear it.’”
